result_semantic_payload.summary:
The seized workstation holds four text files, all created at the same timestamp (1790594136). Two of them directly evidence a payment-collection (收款) operation, one provides supporting platform-operation context, and one is the owner's private medical document that is explicitly unrelated and must be excluded from the payment-collection evidentiary chain.

PAYMENT-COLLECTION EVIDENCE:
1. /data/收款记录.txt ("Payment Collection Records") — Contains three dated entries documenting USDT payments received from named individuals: (a) 2023-11-02, 陈某 (Chen), 30,000 USDT, bank card 6222020212345678901; (b) 2023-11-04, 周某 (Zhou), 17,500 USDT, wallet 0xDEAD1111; (c) 2023-11-09, 吴某 (Wu), 52,000 USDT, wallet 0xDEAD1111. This file is the primary ledger of the collection operation.

2. /platform/说明.txt ("Platform Notes") — Documents the internal platform name "聚宝盆" (Jubaopen / "Treasure Bowl"), a backend admin URL (http://jbpenl-admin.example), and a daily customer-acquisition quota of 20 new users per customer-service group. This file establishes the operational infrastructure and organizational context behind the payment collection.

EXCLUDED DOCUMENT:
3. /personal/体检报告.txt ("Medical Examination Report") — A sample medical report for 陈某 dated 2023-10-20, noting normal blood pressure and elevated blood lipids. The file's own content states it is unrelated to any financial activity ("与任何资金活动无关"). The README.txt on the device explicitly directs that personal-directory documents "have no evidential relation to the payment operation and must not be cited as evidence of it." This file must stay out of the payment-collection evidentiary chain.

CONTEXTUAL FILE:
4. /README.txt — A seizure manifest that describes the directory structure and evidentiary boundaries of the workstation. It is a guide for investigators, not direct evidence of the payment operation itself, but it establishes the intended scope of the evidentiary chain.

claim_candidates.text: The device holds a payment-collection ledger (/data/收款记录.txt) documenting three USDT transactions between 2023-11-02 and 2023-11-09, totaling 99,500 USDT across three named individuals (陈某, 周某, 吴某), using both a bank card number and a cryptocurrency wallet address.

The payment-collection operation was conducted under an internal platform named '聚宝盆' (Jubaopen) with a backend admin interface at http://jbpenl-admin.example and a daily new-user acquisition quota of 20 per customer-service group.
The file /personal/体检报告.txt is a personal medical examination report for 陈某 that is unrelated to the payment-collection operation and must not be included in the evidentiary chain for that operation.

The README.txt seizure manifest explicitly defines the evidentiary boundary: the /data directory holds payment records, the /platform directory holds platform operation notes, and the /personal directory holds private documents with no evidential relation to the payment operation.

limitations: No Windows registry, event log, prefetch, or amcache artifacts were available — the evidence base consists solely of four text files with no execution traces or system-level corroboration.
All four files share an identical filesystem creation timestamp, so filesystem-level temporal ordering cannot distinguish when individual files were authored.
The task metadata reported no platform scenarios or source scopes, limiting the ability to cross-reference with additional forensic artifacts.
Content-level dates in the payment ledger (November 2023) cannot be independently verified against filesystem timestamps, which all resolve to the same epoch value.
warnings: The file /personal/体检报告.txt must not be cited as evidence of the payment-collection operation. Although it references 陈某 (who also appears in the payment ledger), the file is a personal medical document with no evidential relation to the payment operation, as confirmed by both the file's own content and the README.txt seizure manifest.
